A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Flow framework. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–G are readable and support comparison across wording and layout changes.

before.justification: v1 reports original experiments on Gobang development, website design, and LaTeX Beamer writing, including human evaluations, masked-output robustness tests, and runtime measurements.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and appendix analyses, with revisions to some reported results.

M1.justification: The workflow generation, parallel execution, agent cloning, and updating procedures remain substantively unchanged. However, Section 3 changes the parallelism score used for graph selection to an expression involving a set-valued quantity. The PDFs do not establish whether this represents a changed selection computation or an erroneous formula.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same three designed tasks: Gobang development, conference website design, and reinforcement-learning lecture slides. The slide configurations and masked-output test scenario are retained; no additional dataset or task is evaluated.

E2.justification: AutoGen, MetaGPT, and CAMEL remain the evaluated external comparators, with Flow without updates retained in the relevant comparisons. Newly cited methods such as AFlow are discussed in related work but are not added to experiments.

E3.justification: Task prompts, success metrics, slide configurations, the 50-participant ranking protocol, and the update strategy in Appendix D.4 are unchanged. The main-text specification of GPT-3.5-Turbo matches v1's appendix and does not establish a model change.

E4.justification: Existing qualitative failure analyses receive limited revisions. Section 4.3 now states that one MetaGPT slide output met the page requirement, while Section 4.4 limits AutoGen's incomplete-website description to one attempt. The masked-output robustness experiment and other supplementary analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions report five trials for the relevant task and timing experiments and present runtime means with standard deviations in Table 9. No repeated-run counts or uncertainty-reporting procedures change; revised standard-deviation values are result changes.

E6.justification: Table 9 changes GPT-4o-mini Flow-without-updates runtimes from 22.78 ± 12.45 to 51.98 ± 20.19 for websites and from 44.21 ± 13.67 to 53.19 ± 17.65 for Beamer. Section 4.1 corrects AutoGen's average human rating from 2.75 to 2.63. Some qualitative findings are also revised, while Tables 1–8 retain their numerical results.

T1.justification: Section 3 replaces P_avg = (1/T) sum_t (|S_t|/|V|) with P_avg = (1/T) sum_t S_t, although S_t remains defined as a set. This is not an equivalent mathematical definition and leaves the score ill-defined. Theorem 3.1 and its Appendix G proof otherwise retain their substance with renamed symbols.

C1.justification: The introduction's third contribution drops the explicit claim of experiments 'across multiple datasets', narrowing the stated empirical support. The central claims about modular workflows, dynamic adaptation, efficiency, and error tolerance remain unchanged.

C2.justification: Appendix B.4 removes the explanation attributing GPT-3.5-Turbo's greater update frequency to weaker task execution and insufficient generated data. The adaptability–runtime tradeoff and the context-length and workflow-optimality limitations remain.

D1.justification: v2 adds a code-repository pointer in the abstract and clarifies that role constraints can be specified in prompts. It removes Appendix E.2's dedicated agent-availability and resource-management discussion, including the explicit agent-count bound. These documentation changes do not establish changed execution constraints.

R1.justification: Five cited works are added, including AFlow, Automated Design of Agentic Systems, and LLM-Planner. Section 2 adds a description of AFlow's Monte Carlo tree search and shortens explicit contrasts with earlier graph frameworks. This is a limited expansion and adjustment of research positioning.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction, related work, method explanation, and experimental narrative undergo widespread editing and paragraph rewriting. Terminology is standardized, a method overview is added, and the dictionary description becomes a structured list. The editorial revision is extensive despite retaining the overall section sequence.

P2.justification: Figure 2 is substantially redrawn into initialization, execution, checking, and updating panels. Other figures and tables retain their displays with caption, spacing, and placement adjustments, including regrouping the appendix workflow figures. The expanded Figure 5 caption in v2 intrudes on the page number.

improvement.justification: The clearer workflow illustration, code pointer, broader related work, and corrections to result descriptions improve accessibility and consistency. However, v2 makes the central parallelism score mathematically ambiguous, obscuring how workflows are selected, and removes some resource-management documentation. These competing changes prevent a reliable judgment of net overall improvement from the PDFs.
